items.stem: How should enterprise risk best be communicated to a board of directors?

options.text: Framed as business impact with likelihood, owners and treatment
options.rationale: Correct: boards need risk in business terms, not raw technical counts.

options.text: As a raw list of CVE identifiers
options.rationale: CVE lists are technical detail unsuited to a board audience.

options.text: By withholding residual risk to avoid alarm
options.rationale: Hiding residual risk undermines informed governance.

options.text: As the number of firewall rules changed
options.rationale: That is an activity metric, not business risk.

items.explanation: Correct: boards need risk in business terms, not raw technical counts.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A service must lose no more than 15 minutes of data in a disaster. Which objective does that define?

options.rationale: Correct: RPO is the maximum tolerable data loss measured in time.
RTO is how fast service is restored, not how much data is lost.
MTBF measures reliability, not tolerable data loss.
An SLA is a broader commitment, not this specific data-loss measure.

items.explanation: Correct: RPO is the maximum tolerable data loss measured in time.

items.stem: Which TWO actions belong in the early (preparation and identification) phases of incident management? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Define an incident classification and escalation scheme in advance
options.rationale: Correct: classification/escalation is prepared before incidents occur.

options.text: Establish and test detection and alerting capability
options.rationale: Correct: detection must be in place to identify incidents.

options.text: Permanently delete all logs after any alert
options.rationale: Deleting logs destroys evidence and detection history.

options.text: Pay any ransom immediately without analysis
options.rationale: That is not a sound preparation/identification action.
Reviews belong to the closing phase and must not be skipped.

items.explanation: Correct: classification/escalation is prepared before incidents occur.
